evidence.quote: The report must begin by acknowledging the reality that inflation remains far too high.
It seems to me likely that the ultimate level of rates will need to be somewhat higher than thought at the time of the September meeting and Summary of Economic Projections.
The time for moderating the pace of rate increases may come as soon as the December meeting.
So far, we have seen only tentative signs of moderation of labor demand.
History cautions strongly against prematurely loosening policy. We will stay the course until the job is done.
It will take substantially more evidence to give comfort that inflation is actually declining.

parsed.rationale: The speaker signals a higher terminal rate, rates held restrictive for some time, and forceful concern about inflation and a tight labor market. The hawkish lean is tempered by signaling a slower pace of hikes as soon as December.
